text: One day Paul, the only son, asked his mother why they did not keep a car of their own and why they always used Uncles car or else a taxi. <break time="0.8s" /> Because we are the poorest members of the family, said the mother, and when Paul asked why, she answered bitterly that it was because his father had no luck. <break time="0.8s" /> Is luck money, mother, he asked, and she explained that luck was what caused you to have money, so it was better to be born lucky than rich. <break time="0.8s" /> When the boy asked whether she herself was lucky, she said that she used to think so before she married, but that now she believed she was very unlucky indeed. <break time="0.8s" /> The child looked at her with unsure eyes, then said stoutly, Well, anyhow, I am a lucky person, and when she asked why, he answered, God told me. <break time="0.8s" /> He saw that she did not believe him, or rather, that she paid no attention to his words, and this angered him and made him want to compel her attention. <break time="0.8s" /> He went off by himself, searching for the clue to luck, and he would sit on his big rocking horse, charging madly into space with a frenzy that made his little sisters uneasy. <break time="0.8s" /> Now, he would silently command the snorting steed, Now, take me to where there is luck, and he would strike its neck with his little whip. <break time="0.8s" /> When he finally slid down, he announced fiercely, Well, I got there, and when his mother asked where, he flared back, Where I wanted to go.
